headline: High: Flowise’s default broad network/filesystem access can amplify downstream leakage and workflow errors when paired with a non-networked, unverified agent-hub source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is an agent hub with MCP/RAG tags, so it may emit or route untrusted content; Profile B is a graph-based flow builder that reads files and can run browser/tool nodes. A shared filesystem or file handoff could let attacker-controlled content from A influence B, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are written into a file that B later ingests as flow input
IF B parses A-produced content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable file-based handoff between the agents
Add a provenance banner to all A outputs before B consumes them
Require B to treat A content as untrusted text only
Review any browser/tool node that can execute instructions from content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has no data classes touched and no network egress, while B touches chatflow inputs/outputs, reads/writes files, and has broad network egress. If sensitive material enters B’s workspace, B can transmit it outward; A does not appear to add leakage on its own. The pair risk is therefore driven by B’s default surfaces, with A providing no compensating controls.
conditions: IF sensitive chatflow inputs are stored in B’s server filesystem
IF B flows send file contents to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Restrict B to a private workspace with least-privilege file access
Turn off or gate external HTTP/model tools for sensitive flows
Delete uploaded files immediately after run completion
Separate secrets into a dedicated vault outside chatflow storage
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing and retention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes no write or network capabilities in the profile, but B can write the filesystem and shares state via a server datastore across instances. Because A is unverified and may still produce artifacts consumed by B, the main conflict is B’s mutable shared state rather than direct overlap. Uncertainty about A’s hidden surfaces means we should not downgrade below medium.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory or datastore
IF multiple B instances operate on the same chatflow run state
mitigations: Assign each run a unique workspace directory
Disable concurrent edits to the same chatflow
Snapshot state before B writes shared artifacts
Use file locks or datastore row locks
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control to shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an unverified agent hub and B is a multi-agent orchestrator that can act on tools and external APIs. If B treats A’s generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into browser/API actions or persisted flows. Because B’s defaults include action-capable tooling and A lacks verification, the blast radius can be irreversible, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced text as a source of truth without validation
IF B’s flow includes tool nodes that send emails, API calls, or file writes based on A output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any B action node
Require citations or schema validation on A outputs
Mark A outputs as advisory, not authoritative
Log and diff A-to-B transformations before execution
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and action

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and touches no data classes, while B explicitly handles chatflow inputs/outputs, model keys, tool credentials, and server files. The pair creates a compliance surface around retention and secrets handling, but no residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. This is a policy-gap risk rather than a direct legal breach, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B’s chatflows
IF B retains uploaded files or logs longer than the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B flows
Rotate and vault model-provider keys separately from chatflow data
Set short retention for uploads and logs
Document a deletion/export process for chatflow artifacts
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
